item.text: {"summary":"A low-growing, hairless perennial flowering plant native to Europe and Western Asia, lesser celandine has fleshy, heart-shaped dark green leaves and glossy bright yellow flowers. It emerges in late winter and can form extensive carpets; in North America it is introduced and invasive. Raw plants are poisonous, but cooking or drying removes toxicity, and Mesolithic Europeans ate the roots boiled, fried or roasted.","humanEdibility":"yes","edibilityNote":"Cooked or dried plants have been eaten; Mesolithic Europeans ate roots boiled, fried or roasted.
